doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Pop music tastes: Motown and horn groups
summary: He liked Motown and oldies from his sister's records and horn bands such as Chicago, while staying chiefly a jazz fan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Okay so I’m trying to think what the pop music at the time might have been.
Oh that influenced me? © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
I mean did you get into pop music also?

I mean to an extent, yeah. I mean I wasn’t a total jazz nerd, but yeah, I mean I liked some of the Motown stuff because my sister was a bit older than me and had a lot of Motown records around the house, and some oldies rock we had around the house, you know, again, stuff that was before my time but that was some of the things I was interested in as far as pop music.
What about, did you happen to get into groups like Chicago or BS&T that had horn sections?
Yeah, I did like those, and I’ve always enjoyed those kind of groups too. Fun music. They always had good horn players.
But you were still a jazzer from an early age.
Yeah. I mean that was the thing I was most interested in, but I’ve always been pretty open minded and listened to a lot of different things, from classical to some pop to whatever.
